slides: Let's continue, with primes in a factorial.

slides.say: Now a question about dividing a factorial. For that, we break every factor into primes, like in the primes topic.
Six factorial is six times five times four times three times two times one.
Six is two times three, and four is two times two.
Let's count the twos. One in the six, two in the four, and one in the two. That's four twos.
The threes are in the six and in the three, so two threes. And one five.
So six factorial is two to the power of four, times three squared, times five.
at: two to the power of four

slides.say: Let's check. Sixteen times nine is a hundred forty-four. Times five, it's seven hundred twenty.
Is six factorial divisible by thirty-two? Thirty-two is two to the power of five. But we have only four twos, so no.
at: Is six factorial divisible by thirty-two

slides.say: Is it divisible by forty-five? Forty-five is three squared times five. We have both, so yes.
Careful here. A lot of students count the even numbers. There are three even numbers, six, four and two. But there are four twos, because four hides two of them.
Seven factorial is the same, times one more prime, seven.
And a last fact, rare on the exam. Three factorial times two to the power of three is six times eight, forty-eight.
And two times four times six is also forty-eight.
Why? Give each factor of three factorial its own two. One times two, two times two, and three times two. That's two, four and six.
at: One times two, two times two

slides.say: So k factorial times two to the power of k is the product of the even numbers from two up to two k.
at: the product of the even numbers

slides.say: So let's sum it up. Know a hundred twenty, seven hundred twenty and five thousand forty by sight.
Expand a factorial only as far as you need.
A big factorial over a smaller one is a run of neighbours.
For a sum or a difference, take out the smaller factorial, and don't forget the one.
And for dividing, count the primes. Take a moment to memorize this, and I'll see you in the next video.
